exposure: systolic blood pressure (sBP) at 8-11, 12-15, and 16-19 weeks of gestation
diastolic blood pressure (dBP) at 8-11, 12-15, and 16-19 weeks of gestation
cohort: The study included 215 women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with essential hypertension either before or within 14 weeks of gestation.
finding: Systolic blood pressure (sBP) less than 130 mmHg within 14 weeks of gestation was associated with a reduced risk of developing early-onset superimposed preeclampsia in women with chronic hypertension.
